slides.title: 4 prompts for when a client **hasn't paid you**
slides.sub: Copy, fill in the brackets, send. Save this for the next late invoice.

slides.title: The invoice email
slides.prompt: Write a short email to send with invoice #[number] for $[amount] for [project]. Include the due date of [date], accepted payment methods: [list], and a thank-you line.
slides.tip: a clear email gets paid faster than a bare attachment.

slides.title: The friendly reminder
slides.prompt: Write a friendly reminder for invoice #[number], which was due [X] days ago. Assume it was an oversight. Include the amount and how to pay. Under 60 words.
slides.tip: most late payments are forgotten, not refused.

slides.title: The firm second reminder
slides.prompt: Write a second reminder for invoice #[number], now [X] days overdue. Stay polite but firm, say I'll pause further work until it's paid, and give a clear deadline.
slides.tip: a deadline turns a request into a decision.

slides.title: Ask for a deposit next time
slides.prompt: A new client hasn't paid a deposit yet. Write a short message that explains my standard [X]% deposit, why I use it, and how to pay, so I can book their start date.
slides.tip: the best late-payment fix is a deposit upfront.
